query: I live and work from home in Victoria for a company headquartered in New South Wales. My contract calls me a permanent employee of the NSW company, but I visit Sydney about once a month. After I reported anxiety caused by workload and lodged a workers' compensation claim, the company dismissed me for alleged poor performance. It says NSW policies apply because payroll and management are there. Please separate the Commonwealth employment-law issues from the applicable State workers' compensation and workplace-safety issues, explain which jurisdiction governs each, and give me a practical action plan for any overlapping deadlines.

I live in Queensland and bought a home solar battery online from a Victorian company. Its Queensland contractor installed the system at my house, but it repeatedly shuts down and has scorched part of the garage wall. The seller says its Victorian terms limit me to repair and require all disputes to be brought in Melbourne, while the installer says any safety or licensing issue is for Queensland authorities. What rights and remedies might I have, which parts are Commonwealth or Queensland law, and where could I pursue the seller and installer?

My company proposes a mineral-processing facility in Western Australia near habitat used by a threatened species. We have received preliminary support from the local council, and a consultant says Commonwealth environmental approval may also be required. The board wants to know whether approval at one level removes the need for approval at the other. Please provide an issue-spotting analysis of the separate Commonwealth, Western Australian, and local approval tracks, the legal risk of starting early works, and the order in which we should address them.

I operate an Australian health app through a private company based in Victoria. A cloud-account compromise exposed medical notes and identity documents belonging to patients in Victoria and Tasmania. Some records came from Victorian clinics, while Tasmanian patients entered others directly into the app. I need a prioritized 72-hour response plan identifying any Commonwealth privacy and data-breach obligations, any State health-record or privacy regimes that may operate alongside them, and which regulators or affected people may need to be notified. Please do not assume that one privacy regime displaces all the others.

I work in Canberra for a national retailer and believe I was denied promotion because I am pregnant. Human resources says I can use either a Commonwealth discrimination process or an ACT process but cannot explain the differences. Compare the possible federal and ACT pathways, including remedies, procedural risks, election or duplication issues, and the information I should gather before choosing one.

I live and run my consultancy in New South Wales. A Victorian publisher uploaded an article from Melbourne accusing me of falsifying client records, and people read it across Australia. Most of my clients are in Sydney, but the publisher's witnesses and documents are in Victoria. Please analyse which law may govern an online defamation claim, whether the nationally uniform legislation means the State is irrelevant, where proceedings could be brought, and what limitation or pre-action questions depend on the forum.

I live in the ACT and am employed by a labour-hire business managed from New South Wales. During the last year it sent me on projects in Queensland and the Northern Territory; I was injured during a six-week assignment in Darwin. My employer says I must claim in NSW because that is where my contract and payroll are kept, while the site operator says the NT scheme applies. How should the applicable workers' compensation system be identified, can more than one scheme apply, and what facts and urgent steps matter?

My Victorian company plans to buy a hotel in New South Wales and a warehouse in Queensland under one sale agreement. The directors assume that registering the company and signing the agreement in Victoria means Victorian property and duty law governs both acquisitions. Is that correct? Please map which land, conveyancing, registration, and transfer-duty questions must be considered separately for each property, and identify any Commonwealth corporate issues that genuinely operate across the transaction.

My former de facto partner and I have always lived in Western Australia. We separated after 12 years and disagree about our Perth home, superannuation, a business held in my partner's name, and arrangements for our eight-year-old child. A friend told me de facto property disputes and parenting cases are all governed by the same federal family-law system throughout Australia. Please explain whether that is accurate for Western Australia, separate the property and parenting issues, identify the appropriate court or courts, and list the first steps I should take.

I have received two government decisions: a Commonwealth decision cancelling my visa and a New South Wales decision suspending my occupational licence. Both letters say I have review rights, but the bodies and deadlines are different. Explain why the decisions do not follow one general Australian administrative-review path, identify the federal and NSW review routes separately, and give me a checklist of the documents and dates I should verify immediately.

I sent repeated threatening messages from South Australia to a former business partner in Tasmania using a social-media service. Tasmania Police have contacted me, and I have also been told that using an online communications service may attract a Commonwealth offence. Which jurisdiction's criminal law could apply, can State and Commonwealth offences operate on the same conduct, and what should I do before an interview?

I am a subcontractor on a commercial construction project in Queensland. My company and the head contractor are incorporated in New South Wales, and our contract selects NSW law, but all work, progress claims, and alleged defects arose in Queensland. I also registered a security interest over supplied equipment under the national personal-property securities system. The head contractor says the NSW choice-of-law clause lets it ignore Queensland security-of-payment and licensing rules. Please assess that position, distinguish the Commonwealth and State regimes, and explain the forums, deadlines, and evidence that may matter.

I hold a Commonwealth licence authorising my business to provide a regulated service throughout Australia, but a new Victorian law prohibits one part of the service. Does the federal licence automatically override the Victorian prohibition? I want a substantial analysis of constitutional inconsistency, including the difference between a Commonwealth permission and a positive right, whether complying with both laws is possible, and what facts or statutory wording would determine the result.

A former contractor copied the source code and graphics from my Australian company's app and is selling a competing version online. Our written agreement describes the work and fees but says nothing about copyright ownership. I have not said which State I am in. Can you still analyse ownership, infringement, remedies, and urgent steps, or does Australian federalism make my State essential?

I own 30% of an Australian proprietary company. The two directors have issued shares to themselves at a large discount, diverted a company opportunity, and refused access to financial records. I want to know about directors' duties, shareholder oppression, possible remedies, and urgent orders. No State is specified because I want you to identify whether these are principally Commonwealth corporations-law questions and whether any missing location fact is actually necessary before giving useful advice.

My negligence case is being heard in Queensland and turns on a common-law duty question for which neither side has found a Queensland appellate decision. The other side relies on a recent unanimous New South Wales Court of Appeal decision on almost identical facts. I rely on an older Victorian Court of Appeal decision pointing the other way and a broader High Court decision that does not address this exact situation. Which decisions bind the Queensland court, what persuasive weight should the interstate appellate decisions receive, and how should the conflict be resolved within the common law of Australia?

I rent an apartment somewhere in Australia. The owner has given me seven days to leave, kept my bond, and says I must pay for replacing worn carpet. What are my rights and which tribunal should I use?

I was badly injured in a supermarket fall about two and a half years ago, but I have not said where in Australia it happened. I want to know whether the supermarket was negligent, how long I have to sue, and what court or pre-court process applies. Please tell me what jurisdictional information you need before analysing the claim.
